editorial_plan.report_thesis: The benchmark shows that app acquisition and engagement patterns vary by vertical and region, supporting a category-specific reading of performance alongside the report’s recommendation for integrated measurement to inform optimization and budget allocation.

themes.theme: Market scale and outlook: the report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Global 2025 acquisition and usage diverged in both categories: e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%, and finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Global gaming growth varied by subvertical from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Global all-games gaming retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025, with day 1 retention at 27% and day 30 at 5%; separately, overall global gaming app CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI moved down from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while CPI for the deal discovery category rose from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: for 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025, with North America highest among regions at 8.43 minutes, LATAM rising to 5.87 minutes, and declines from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data; this is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

summary.card_tldr_compact: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025.
summary.executive_summary: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025. In 2025, consumer spending in the mobile-app market rose 10.6% year over year to $167 billion. In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year and sessions rose 5% year over year; global finance app installs fell 4% year over year and sessions rose 21% year over year. Globally, gaming app growth from 2024 to 2025 varied by subvertical: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%. The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data.

expert_comment: In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% year over year while sessions rose 21%. Global e-commerce app CPI declined from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while deal discovery CPI increased from $1.44 to $2.26. The implication is that acquisition alone and the all-e-commerce CPI measure each give an incomplete view: session direction diverged from installs in e-commerce and finance, while deal discovery CPI moved opposite to the all-e-commerce figure. For budget reviews, MarketLense would pair category-level install, session, and CPI views with integrated measurement rather than rely on any one signal.
linkedin_post:
Global finance app installs fell 4% year over year in 2025, while sessions rose 21%. Acquisition and usage moved in opposite directions.

That distinction matters when describing performance: install volume alone does not capture the reported session trend.

MarketLense’s recommendation: when assessing finance-app performance, keep installs and sessions as separate measures.

decision_brief.strategic_context: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, reported as having occurred rather than as a forecast.
decision_implications: The report pairs reported 2025 activity and spending with a separate longer-term economic projection.
Install and session trends diverged in both categories, so acquisition volume alone does not describe reported usage.
Aggregate gaming results can obscure differences between subverticals and between acquisition and engagement.
priority_moves: Use these as market context while distinguishing reported outcomes from the 2030 projection.
Track installs and sessions as separate measures when assessing category performance.
Compare installs and sessions at the subvertical level rather than relying on a single gaming-wide growth rate.
watchouts: Globally, all-games gaming app retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025: day 1 retention was 27% and day 30 retention was 5%. Global gaming app CPI rose to $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.

items.recommendation: Use these as market context while distinguishing reported outcomes from the 2030 projection.
Track installs and sessions as separate measures when assessing category performance.
Compare installs and sessions at the subvertical level rather than relying on a single gaming-wide growth rate.
Assess retention and CPI together when evaluating gaming acquisition efficiency.
Review CPI by e-commerce subcategory when evaluating acquisition costs and budget allocation.
Compare finance performance by region and metric rather than treating a single regional result as representative.
Consider an integrated measurement foundation that supports attribution, AI-assisted analysis, optimization, and budget decisions.

claim_ledgers.claim_text: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025.
In 2025, consumer spending in the mobile-app market rose 10.6% year over year to $167 billion.
In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% year over year while sessions rose 21%.

Globally, gaming app growth from 2024 to 2025 varied by subvertical: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data.

The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% year over year while sessions rose 21%.

Globally, gaming app install and session growth varied by subvertical year over year from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy installs declined 1% while sessions grew 57%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Globally, all-games gaming app retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025: day 1 retention was 27% and day 30 retention was 5%. Global gaming app CPI rose to $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI declined from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while deal discovery CPI increased from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: in 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. North America had the highest regional session length at 8.43 minutes, while LATAM rose to 5.87 minutes and session length declined in APAC from 7.07 to 6.94 minutes, Europe from 5.77 to 5.62 minutes, and MENA from 6.61 to 6.39 minutes.

The report recommends an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation for app marketers, combining cross-channel attribution to remove blind spots and expose trends, AI insights for faster and more effective analysis, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and confident budget allocation based on aggregated data. This is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

planned_themes: Market scale and outlook: the report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Global 2025 acquisition and usage diverged in both categories: e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%, and finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Global gaming growth varied by subvertical from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Global all-games gaming retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025, with day 1 retention at 27% and day 30 at 5%; separately, overall global gaming app CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI moved down from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while CPI for the deal discovery category rose from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: for 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025, with North America highest among regions at 8.43 minutes, LATAM rising to 5.87 minutes, and declines from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data; this is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

findings.text: For finance apps, global session length increased 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. In 2025, North America had the highest regional session length at 8.43 minutes, and LATAM rose to 5.87 minutes. Session length declined from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

planned_themes: Market scale and outlook: the report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Global 2025 acquisition and usage diverged in both categories: e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%, and finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Global gaming growth varied by subvertical from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Global all-games gaming retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025, with day 1 retention at 27% and day 30 at 5%; separately, overall global gaming app CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI moved down from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while CPI for the deal discovery category rose from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: for 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025, with North America highest among regions at 8.43 minutes, LATAM rising to 5.87 minutes, and declines from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data; this is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.
